comment: Terminal-path behavior parity manifest (#257).
Nightgauge has two pipeline execution paths that must stay behavior-parallel:
Go:        Scheduler.runPipeline() via dispatchItem (CLI/auto mode, autonomous board-scan)
Extension: queue.dequeueIndependent over IPC -> ConcurrentPipelineManager.fillSlots -> HeadlessOrchestrator
A behavior wired to only one path is invisible on the other: no error, no failed test,
no log line (#210 stage gates, #254 CompleteQueueItem).
Every behavior a dispatched run must perform when it reaches a terminal state is listed
here, with the call-site anchor on each path, or an explicit pathSpecific reason (and,
where the gap is a defect, the tracking issue). Two test suites enforce this manifest —
internal/orchestrator/terminal_parity_test.go and
packages/nightgauge-vscode/tests/services/terminalParity.test.ts:
1. every anchor listed here must exist in its file (a rename/removal fails both suites);
2. the fenced terminal-funnel regions (terminal-parity markers in scheduler.go and
ConcurrentPipelineManager.ts) are content-pinned by sha256 of their normalized source.
ANY change inside a fence fails the tests until the hash here is updated — that is
the point: updating this file is the moment you answer 'which of the two paths
reaches the behavior I just added, and is the other one intentionally excluded?'
A behavior row may carry an `accounting` array (see force-clear-terminal-bookkeeping): a
line-by-line reconciliation of that row against EVERY other behavior in this file. Use it
when a row describes a SECOND funnel on one path — a partial enumeration presented as
complete is exactly the silent divergence this manifest exists to prevent.
To update a fence hash after a deliberate change: run the failing test; it prints the
new hash. Record it here together with any behavior rows the change added or removed.
Normalization (identical in both suites): per line, trim whitespace; drop empty lines;
drop lines starting with '//'; join with '\n'; sha256 hex.

behaviors.name: board-status-failure-sync
behaviors.note: Terminal board status intentionally differs today: Go moves to Ready/Backlog (FailPipeline), the extension moves to In review with the autonomous layer re-reverting to Ready. Parity here asserts both paths sync SOMETHING, not that the target status matches.

behaviors.name: learning-outcome-record
behaviors.note: Wired on both paths as of #304, and rooted identically — the corpus is written to the run's TARGET repo on both paths (#215/#232), never the daemon launch root or the IPC server's mutable active-repo pointer. The extension side records at the Go side of its terminal funnel (pipeline.notifyComplete), deriving the outcome from the same V2 run record it writes — the Go scheduler's recordOutcome is unreachable from the extension path. SKIP PARITY: both paths record NOTHING for a blocked-dependency deferral (#305) and a network_unavailable failure (#3296). The scheduler keys both on terminal_failure_kind; the extension keys the deferral on record.outcome_type (which #305 sets from the wire flag and which clears terminal_failure_kind) and the network case on terminal_failure_kind. Same two states, different fields, because the deferral override on the extension path erases the kind.

extension.pathSpecific: NOT WIRED — the extension path leaves orphaned remote branches to the Go-side reconcile/worktree sweeps (#110 lineage) instead of reclaiming at terminal time. Revisit if sweep coverage changes.

Intentionally different mechanism: the extension preserves a failed run's worktree (cleanupSlot preserveWorktree) rather than deleting it, so recover-before-cleanup does not apply. The Go path deletes worktrees on every terminal outcome (#106) and must recover first (#3542/#3365).

behaviors.name: run-scoped-attention
behaviors.note:
WIRED ON BOTH PATHS as of #305. The extension raises through the `attention.raise` IPC verb, whose handler builds the card with the SAME exported orchestrator builders the Go scheduler calls (BuildBudgetCeilingHit / BuildBranchProtectionBlock) and writes it through the SAME single authoritative store — so dedup by idempotency_key, standing-fingerprint semantics, the journal, the attention.event push, and resolve/verb execution are inherited, not reimplemented. The verb takes a CLOSED producer id plus typed scalars: it carries no options, no verb, and no args map, because card options are EXECUTED by the daemon on resolve and a free-form raise would let any surface mint a plausible card offering an arbitrary operation. Both halves of the parity are tested — internal/orchestrator TestRunScopedProducersDelegateToSharedBuilders pins the scheduler call site to the builder, internal/ipc TestAttentionRaiseProducesTheGoPathCard pins the IPC path to the same builder.

NO NUMBER CROSSES THE WIRE, AND THE STATE IT IS DERIVED FROM CANNOT BE MINTED BY THE RAISER (security fix, rounds 2-4). The budget-ceiling card's primary option persists a per-repo runtime ceiling override on resolve, so the enforced ceiling and the run's spend are derived DAEMON-SIDE — the ceiling in-process via orchestrator.PipelineBudgetCeilingUSD (the same read scheduler.go does), the spend from the run's own recorded RuntimeState. Round 3 stopped at 'derived daemon-side' and left the derivation forgeable: the runtime map is filled by pipeline.notifyStageTransition, which CREATES an entry when none exists, so ONE call minted a $1e6 run and the next raise built a $1.5M raiseCeiling option out of it. Corroboration is now narrower on both arms (live runtime and persisted runtime-{N}.json): the record's repo must EQUAL the raise's repo — an empty one corroborates nothing, the same call #307 made when it refused to persist an unattributed runtime — and the figure is summed over CompletedStages the daemon watched BEGIN (non-zero StartedAt, stamped only by the 'running' transition's BeginStage), never off the TotalCostUSD accumulator. A created-on-miss terminal transition books a stage with a zero StartedAt and corroborates nothing. When the spend cannot be corroborated the card is still raised but WITHOUT the raiseCeiling option, and the repo must be one this daemon has configured. See ADR-015 §N for the trust model this sits inside and its residual exposure (#370). The remedy also has to WORK on the extension path, which it did not at first: getPipelineCeilingConfig now reads .nightgauge/pipeline/budget-override.json with Go's max(config, override) rule, and BOTH sides resolve that file under the RUN'S OWN REPO ROOT — HeadlessOrchestrator.getRunRepoRoot() on the read, Server.repoRoot(repo) on the raise and the resolve. Round 3 read workspaceFolders[0] and wrote s.workspaceRoot (a pointer that follows the focused editor), so in a multi-repo workspace neither was the run's repo and the remedy was inert again.

TWO of the six run-scoped producers are wired; the other FOUR are deferred with reasons. budget-ceiling (the anchor below) and branch-protection fire from HeadlessOrchestrator. abandoned-dispatch is NOT one of the six — it is extension-only with no Go counterpart, so it neither adds to the wired count nor subtracts from the deferred one (see its own row). The deferred four are auth-preflight, branch-fork, unverified-deliverable and unverified-deliverable-streak; round 3 counted the streak as part of its parent and the arithmetic came out as three and three. DECLARED ASYMMETRY on budget-ceiling: HeadlessOrchestrator has THREE pipeline-ceiling stops and only the BETWEEN-STAGE one raises. The pre-stage hard stop (preCheck.shouldStop, 'refusing to start <stage>') and the mid-stage hard stop (ceilingCheck.shouldStop && !budgetTerminated) both terminate on the same ceiling and card nothing — setOutcomeType('budget-ceiling') appears at exactly one line. Not fixed here because the other two stops end the run through paths whose terminal funnel is not this one, and wiring a raise into each without tracing that funnel is how one condition becomes three cards. Declared rather than left silent, against this manifest's own standard. DECLARED ASYMMETRY on branch-protection: the Go path's DeterministicRunner.Run responds to MergeBlockedByPendingCI by WAITING out the bounded CI budget and re-Deciding, so a block that only becomes visible once a required check FAILS still gets carded there. The extension's fallback takes ONE `gh pr view` sample with no CI wait and never re-samples, so that same late-emerging block is never carded on the extension path. Suppressing the card for an undetermined condition is the right call (a card would be a confident wrong diagnostic), but the coverage it costs is declared here rather than left silent. DEFERRED (4): auth-preflight (the extension's analogues are network-vs-auth heuristics, not the fail-closed definitive block Go raises on); branch-fork (not detected on the extension path at all — needs the BranchFork probe ported first); unverified-deliverable and its streak counterpart (the derivation already runs in Go via `nightgauge gate verify feature-validate --record`, so the right seam is for THAT CLI to raise — routing it back through IPC would make the extension re-classify a finding Go already classified, the exact duplication deriveUnexercisedDeliverable's own doc comment warns against).

behaviors.name: abandoned-dispatch-attention
behaviors.note:
EXTENSION-ONLY BY DESIGN (#305, closing the gap #307 named). A dispatch the abort deadline force-cleared is booked as terminal but reported nothing durable — its only surfacing was a transient Stop toast and a warn log, and #307's own ledger listed run-scoped-attention as the reason. Both arms of the force-clear funnel now raise the card, so a wedge inside worktree creation is as visible as one mid-stage.

AN INFORMATIONAL STOP CARD, NOT AN UNBLOCK (re-shaped in review once the population was traced). forceClearStuckSlots has exactly ONE call site — abortAll's ABORT_ALL_TIMEOUT_MS branch — and abortAll is reached only from nightgauge.stopPipeline, nightgauge.abortPipeline and deactivate(). Before the deadline can fire, abortAll has already cleared the queue and set userCancelled on every slot, and the terminal error booked is literally `Cancelled by user`, which is why the row below records that an operator Stop books as a generic failure on BOTH paths. So one hundred percent of this producer's population is `the operator pressed Stop and a slot took longer than the deadline to settle`. The first cut emitted kind=unblock, severity=blocking_run and a StylePrimary Retry that cleared the issue's failure cooldown and re-dispatched: stopping three wedged pipelines produced three blocking_run cards each recommending the operator undo their own Stop, at a severity ADR-015 §I routes to alerting while nothing was blocked. The card is now approve/fyi with two noop options, naming only what is true FOR THE SITUATION IT DESCRIBES.

THREE SITUATIONS, THREE BODIES, ONE PRODUCER (fixed in round 4). Round 3 emitted a single fixed body for a producer with three populations, and it was false for two of them. The `situation` field on attention.raise is a closed enum — reservation-never-started | slot-worktree-preserved | claim-taken-then-wedged — that selects PROSE and nothing else: the option set, kind, severity, key and expiry are identical in all three, so no caller-supplied value can change what a card can DO. It is required and rejected when unrecognised rather than defaulted, because a default prints a confident wrong body. (a) reservation-never-started: the dispatch wedged inside startSlotInner (worktree-manager resolution, a 15s git ls-remote, git worktree add), so NO stage ran, nothing was written and notifyStageTransition never fired — round 3 told that operator their worktree 'may hold uncommitted work' and that the Go-side state 'may be stale', both impossible. (b) slot-worktree-preserved: a real slot whose terminal outcome this funnel booked; the preserved worktree and the possibly-stale Go state are the true residue. (c) claim-taken-then-wedged: the dispatch had CLAIMED its own outcome, so step 2 stood down and nobody booked it — the queue mark is released but the Go scheduler's seat is NOT, and isRunning() keeps the issue ineligible for re-dispatch. Round 3's body told that operator 'NOTHING IS BLOCKED and no action is required' in the one case where something was held; the body now names the held seat and what clears it (the wedged process settling, or a scheduler restart). Severity stays fyi in all three: every card here follows the operator's own Stop, and ADR-015 §I routes blocking_run to alerting.

SUPPRESSED ONLY BY A TERMINAL OUTCOME CALLBACK THAT ACTUALLY FIRED — `slot.ownTerminalOutcomeBooked` / `reservation.ownTerminalOutcomeBooked`, set immediately after a terminal outcome callback returns, NOT the `terminalOutcomeDispatched` claim that gates step 2 of the bookkeeping. (Precisely: on the SLOT arm only the dispatch's own callbacks set the flag; on the RESERVATION arm `claimReservationOutcome` sets it and `bookForceClearedReservation` calls that, so the force-clear can set it too. The property both arms share — and the only one the card depends on — is that the flag is READ into a local before any claim of ours fires, so a force-clear never suppresses its own card.) The claim is taken at terminal boundary 1 BEFORE `await slot.stateService.getState()` and the callback fires after it, so a run that wedges in that window holds the claim while having reported nothing at all: no autonomousComplete, the Go scheduler's running-slot seat still held, the queue mark the only bookkeeping performed. Gating the card on the claim silenced exactly that case end to end, which is what #305 exists to stop. A dispatch that genuinely booked its own outcome and merely wedged in post-terminal teardown sets the new flag and gets no card — that is a different condition with no producer today. NOTE the residual hole in the claimed-then-wedged interleaving: the card is raised, but no terminal outcome is booked by anyone (step 2 stands down on the claim), so the Go seat stays held. Still owned by #307/#370 — what round 4 changed is that the card now SAYS so, instead of asserting the opposite. See the claim-taken-then-wedged situation above.

RAISED CONCURRENTLY WITH completeQueueItem, never chained after it. Both are IPC round-trips bounded by IpcClientBase's request timeout (30s by default) and the daemon is unresponsive by definition when this deadline fires; serialising them would double the window in which isShuttingDown makes IssueQueueService refuse every enqueue — the #3111 condition forceClearStuckSlots' own doc comment bounds, arriving through a change made inside the fix for it.

Keyed per (repo, issue) and EVENT-shaped: a slot that wedges, is re-queued, and wedges again collapses onto one card via Store.Raise's open-record dedup. NOT standing — standing would inherit ADR-015 §M suppression (a raise whose fingerprint matches the latest human-RESOLVED record for the key writes nothing), and with a constant fingerprint, no pruning of resolved records and no auto-resolve call site, the operator's FIRST dismissal silenced that issue permanently. The card deliberately carries NO run_id — at force-clear time Go mints the RunID and the extension has no verb to ask for one, and the wedged run's run-state.json may already be archived; an empty run id is a handled case daemon-side, and synthesising one would put a fabricated identity into the audit trail. #370 is what improves this later.

go.pathSpecific: By design extension-only: the Go scheduler's terminal defer runs in the same goroutine as its stage loop, so nothing else can declare a run abandoned while that defer is still owed. There is no Go force-clear funnel, and therefore no Go condition to card.

behaviors.name: terminal-kind-classification
behaviors.note:
ONE TABLE, THREE INTERPRETERS (#306). Terminal-kind classification is no longer written down three times: the ordered rule table lives at internal/terminalkind/table.json, Go embeds it (internal/terminalkind, which orchestrator.ClassifyTerminalKind delegates to as a body-checked one-line delegation), and packages/nightgauge-sdk/src/analysis/health/terminalKindTable.generated.ts is GENERATED from it by `make generate-terminal-kind-table`. The SDK's classifyTerminalKind and the extension's classifyTerminalKindForSignal both interpret that generated table. Before this there were three hand-written ladders held aligned by comments, disagreeing on 19 of 98 real and synthetic inputs.

THE SIGNAL SIDE CANNOT OVERRIDE THE RECORD, WITH ONE DECLARED EXCEPTION. Go's NotifyComplete uses a non-empty kind from the extension VERBATIM, so the extension runs the FULL ladder and projects the winning rule only when that rule is declared `signal: true`. On every RULE its answer is therefore either nothing or exactly what Go records — bounded above and below, per row, by `expected_signal` in the shared corpus. The exception is the table's `signal_extensions` section: reaction-only rules, consulted ONLY when the rule ladder projects no SIGNAL, so an extension can never overrule a kind projected by a `signal: true` RULE — the widest it can reach is text the signal SUBSET ignores. A kind the record names through a NON-signal rule is not protected, and that is not hypothetical. There is exactly one extension today — session-usage-limit-quota, the #3792 defense-in-depth for an Anthropic/Codex session-or-usage-limit line — and it covers BOTH cases: a bare quota line, which no rule classifies at all, and a quota line that NAMES A MODEL, which the non-signal model-unavailable rule classifies, so the record says model_unavailable and the fleet reacts rate_limit_quota_exhausted. That pair is main's exact behaviour, and of round 2's two record-vs-reaction divergences it is the one that did NOT dissolve: it is now declared as data with a written reason and pinned by the corpus rows order-model-unavailable-beats-quota-wording and model-unavailable-predicate-by-model-id, whose expected_signal differs from expected. (The other — an overload carrying an explicit quota marker — did dissolve under one table with one precedence.) The corpus well-formedness test permits expected_signal != expected for declared extensions and for nothing else; a further test requires every extension CLAUSE to be necessary to such a row; another requires every `~` word-bounded term to have a row that moves when its boundary is dropped, with a derived input and corpus rows for EACH EDGE independently (the boundary is a conjunction of two tests, and sampling only the right edge left the left conjunct deletable in one line with every suite green and every artifact byte-identical); and the ORDER of the projection's two stages — rule ladder first, extensions second, which is the only thing that makes the bound above true — is pinned by inputs carrying BOTH a signal marker and extension wording, since without them reversing the two blocks of SignalKind moved no answer anywhere.

WHAT IS PINNED, AND BY WHAT. (1) Behaviour: internal/terminalkind/testdata/corpus.json — every row carries a mandatory written rationale — read by internal/terminalkind/corpus_test.go, packages/nightgauge-sdk/tests/analysis/health/terminalKind.corpusParity.test.ts and packages/nightgauge-vscode/tests/services/terminalKindSignal.corpusParity.test.ts; its core rows are real failure text captured from live telemetry by scripts/capture-terminal-kind-fixture.sh. (2) Conjunctions: TestEveryConjunctionHalfIsPinnedByANegativeRow DERIVES the requirement from the table — for every multi-term clause and every half of it, widening that clause to the half alone must change at least one corpus row's answer — so an AND quietly widened into an OR is red rather than merely diffed. (3) Equivalence: internal/terminalkind/stress.go and its verbatim TypeScript twin derive an input for every clause, every term, BOTH EDGES of every `~` word-bounded term, every signal-extension clause, every ordered rule pair and every `signal: true` rule composed with every extension clause in both orders, FROM the table, and all three suites must reproduce testdata/stress-golden.json, so deleting a clause, dropping one half of a word boundary, swapping two rules or swapping the two stages of the signal projection changes a committed answer. (4) Distribution: the generated SDK module and the golden are byte-compared by TestGeneratedTypeScriptIsInSync / TestStressGoldenIsInSync, .husky/pre-commit and scripts/ci-local.sh, so a consumer cannot be edited on its own. (5) The interpreters themselves: every string literal in the internal/terminalkind package and in the SDK's terminalKind.ts must appear in an explicit allowlist, whole-file and both directions in both languages; so must every rune literal and every IMPORT, because a file fence has an outside and a marker declared in a neighbouring module and merely NAMED in the guarded one introduces no literal at all; the one predicate's registry FIELD reads are pinned as an exact set from a single shared poison fixture that both languages drive; and bootstrap/services.ts — which assembles the value sent over IPC — is asserted to be a bare single-assignment delegation. The perimeter is those four surfaces plus the body of orchestrator.ClassifyTerminalKind; downstream consumers can still override the answer and nothing here claims otherwise. (6) Taxonomy: a TerminalKind constant with no rule and no corpus row is red.

ALSO PINNED NOW: ConcurrentPipelineManager's isTransientNetworkFailureText and the haltQueueOnSlotFailure skip-branches were four more private ladders carrying 'keep aligned' comments; they resolve the kind through the table and test set membership (tests/services/concurrentPipelineManager.haltPolicy.test.ts). One deliberate raw-text condition survives there and is documented in place — the same session/usage-limit wording the signal extension carries, kept as a local queue-halt policy because a halt decision is not a kind.

behaviors.name: terminating-stage-cost-booking
behaviors.note: A failing stage's spend must be booked, not dropped — a run's cost picture is wrong exactly where it matters (the retry decision) otherwise (#293, #146).

extension.pathSpecific: By design Go-only (ADR 013 / #179): decision traces are produced by the deterministic layer; there is no TS producer, and replay reads Go-written journals.

go.pathSpecific: Extension-only UX affordance: the interactive mode posts the failure comment where the operator is looking; the autonomous Go path surfaces failures through attention cards and board state instead.
Extension-only (#3926): auto-retro analysis runs in the interactive mode; the Go path's failures are analyzed by the batch retro skill instead.

behaviors.name: force-clear-terminal-bookkeeping
behaviors.note: SECOND terminal funnel on the extension path (#307), for dispatches that never settle and therefore never reach runSlotPipeline's finally — both slots and stranded reservations. The EXHAUSTIVE per-behavior accounting is in this row's `accounting` field: every behavior in this manifest appears there exactly once, under a labelled disposition (performed / omitted / not-performed / delegated / not-applicable), plus a KNOWN EXPOSURE paragraph for what this change deliberately leaves at main behavior. A partial list presented as complete is the silent divergence this manifest exists to prevent, so when you add a behavior row above, add its disposition here too.
accounting: SECOND terminal funnel on the extension path (#307). abortAll waits 30s for slots to settle; when a
dispatch never settles — a wedged adapter, a stage awaiting an IPC/gh call that ignores the
AbortController, a hung `git worktree add` — the deadline force-clears it. Such a run never reaches
runSlotPipeline's finally, so the funnel above books NOTHING for it; this row is the accounting of
what the force-clear books instead.
TWO ARMS, both inside this fence:
SLOTS        — bookForceClearedSlot, for a dispatch that became a PipelineSlot.
RESERVATIONS — bookForceClearedReservation, for a dispatch still inside startSlot's worktree
creation. It has no slot, no orchestrator and no state service, but it DOES hold a
Go scheduler seat (AutonomousScheduler.enqueueItem appends to state.Running at
dispatch time), so it books the same queue mark and the same terminal outcome.
EXACTLY-ONCE. Each dispatch has one terminal outcome and two possible claimants (the run itself and
this funnel). The claim — PipelineSlot.terminalOutcomeDispatched / SlotReservation.
terminalOutcomeDispatched — is read and taken in a single synchronous step with no await between the
read and the write, which is atomic on the single-threaded extension host. The force-cleared
run id is then TOMBSTONED permanently, and every terminal boundary in runSlotPipeline (try-block
outcome dispatch, catch, fenced finally) checks the tombstone before doing anything, so a run that
settles an hour later cannot re-book, cannot release a re-queued successor's queue mark, and cannot
delete a successor's worktree.
EVERY behavior in this manifest, accounted for. This list is exhaustive by construction: if you add a
behavior row above, add its disposition here, and keep the section counts summing to 22. TestForceClearAccountingIsExhaustive fails when a name is missing. (22 behaviors + this row.)
PERFORMED (3):
queue-item-completion       — completeQueueItem releases the dequeue's `processing` mark, on BOTH
arms; without it the issue is permanently undispatchable (#254's
outcome through a second door).
autonomous-terminal-notify  — onSlotFailed fires on BOTH arms, so bootstrap's autonomousComplete
frees the Go scheduler's running-slot entry. SKIPPED (not omitted)
when the dispatch already claimed its own outcome and was merely
mid-teardown when the deadline fired: autonomousComplete is not
idempotent — it feeds the cascade breaker and the per-issue lifetime
cap.
worktree-cleanup            — SLOT arm: cleanupSlot(preserveWorktree=true) — state service disposed,
onSlotCleaned fired (tree item + subscriptions released), TREE KEPT. A
killed process may still hold it and uncommitted agent work must
survive (#66); reclaiming the tree is #110's sweep. RESERVATION arm:
nothing to tear down here — the wedged startSlotInner removes its own
partial tree when it unwinds and sees the tombstone.
OMITTED — same gate as the SETTLED Stop All path, which sets slot.userCancelled on every slot (4):
board-status-failure-sync   — both paths gate the In-review safety net on !slot.userCancelled, so
the issue keeps its current status and the operator can resume. If
that gate ever changes, this row changes with it.
merged-branch-cleanup       — deleteMergedBranch is `pipelineSucceeded && !userCancelled`: false
here twice over. The local branch is kept for resume/recovery.
queue-halt-on-failure       — abortAll already cleared the queue; halting a queue the operator just
emptied is a no-op with a modal attached.
failure-issue-comment       — no public comment narrating the operator's own stop.
OMITTED — not reachable from this funnel (6):
stage-gate-evaluation       — per-stage, inside HeadlessOrchestrator. A force-clear happens
between/inside stages and runs no stage.
stage-exit-records          — written by the stage runner at each stage exit, not at run terminal.
auto-retro-on-failure       — runs inside HeadlessOrchestrator's own failure path, which a
never-settling runPipeline never reaches.
terminating-stage-cost-booking — booked by Go's notifyStageTransition 'failed' transition, which a
wedged stage never emits. Spend through the last COMPLETED stage is
already booked; the wedged stage's spend was never reported by
anything, so there is nothing to book, not something withheld. (The
slot arm does read that already-booked total off the state service and
pass it to onSlotFailed, so the Output Window badge and
dashboard.recordHealthSnapshotForRun — gated on costUsd > 0 — behave
as they do on the settled path.)
orphaned-remote-branch-reclaim — already NOT WIRED on the extension path at all (see its row); the
force-clear does not change that.
run-scoped-attention        — the OTHER two run-scoped cards (budget-ceiling, branch-protection)
fire from HeadlessOrchestrator's own ceiling/pr-merge checks, which
a dispatch that never settles never reaches. Not deleted from this
list when #305 added abandoned-dispatch-attention (they are two
different behavior rows) — a force-cleared dispatch still raises
neither, and the honest disposition is 'not reachable from this
funnel', not absence.
PERFORMED (added by #305) (1):
abandoned-dispatch-attention— BOTH arms raise the `abandoned-dispatch` Action Center card through
the `attention.raise` IPC verb, so a force-cleared dispatch survives
the Stop toast. An approve/fyi INFORMATIONAL card with two noop
options — every dispatch that reaches here was cancelled by the
operator, so the card offers no Retry. THREE SITUATIONS, THREE
BODIES (round 4): the required `situation` enum names which of
reservation-never-started / slot-worktree-preserved /
claim-taken-then-wedged this force-clear is, and each body states only
what holds for it — a reservation that wedged in worktree setup has no
uncommitted work and no recorded state to be stale, and a claim-taken
wedge is the one case that must NOT say 'nothing is blocked'. The enum
selects prose only: key, kind, severity and options are identical in
all three. Gated on
`ownTerminalOutcomeBooked` (a terminal outcome CALLBACK that actually
fired), NOT on the `terminalOutcomeDispatched` claim step 2 uses: the
claim is taken before an await and the callback fires after it, so a
run that wedges in that window reported nothing and the card is the
only signal left. Issued CONCURRENTLY with completeQueueItem so the
funnel still pays ONE IPC timeout, not two. Event-shaped and keyed
per (repo, issue), so repeat wedges of one issue collapse onto one
card while a wedge AFTER a human dealt with the last one still
speaks up. Fail-open and never-throwing: a raise failure here would
abort the exactly-once bookkeeping this funnel exists to guarantee.
Carries no run_id. The extension now HOLDS one (ADR-017 step 3 mints a
UUIDv7 per dispatch), so the reason has changed from "there is none"
to "threading the raise's identity is ADR-017 step 7"; the card still
carries none today — see the abandoned-dispatch-attention row.
NOT PERFORMED — real gaps, owned elsewhere (2):
terminal-kind-classification— the error handed to onSlotFailed is byte-identical to the SETTLED Stop
All path's (`Cancelled by user`), which neither classifier matches, so
an operator Stop books as a generic failure on BOTH paths.
Deliberately not fixed here: marking only the wedged variant would
make the two Stop paths disagree about what a Stop costs, and the
classifier ladders are #306's scope.
uncommitted-work-recovery   — the wedged process may still be writing in the worktree, so
stashing/committing it is unsafe. Preserving the tree keeps the work
intact; recovery happens at reclamation time.
DELEGATED — produced later, by an existing subsystem (5):
history-record-write        — Go's pipeline.notifyComplete is the sole writer and is unreachable for
learning-outcome-record       a run whose promise never settles. If the run later settles, its own
notifyComplete reaches Go and writes BOTH — see KNOWN EXPOSURE below
for what happens when a successor holds the issue key by then.
pipeline-done-telemetry     — the force-clear cannot emit it. (ADR-017 step 3 changed WHY: the
extension now mints the id, so "Go mints the RunID and the extension has
no verb to ask for one" no longer holds — but there is still no verb that
emits a terminal event for an abandoned dispatch. `pipeline.abandonRun`
is that verb and it lands in step 6.) #44 orphan reconciliation emits it
from the PRESERVED runtime-{issue}-{runId}.json AT THE NEXT SERVER
START, and only there:
reconcileOrphanedRuns' skipIssue is `_, live := s.activeRuntimes[key];
return live`, and the force-clear's only IPC calls (queue.complete,
autonomous.complete) never touch activeRuntimes, so the dead run's
activeRuntimes entry survives for the life of the server and the
workspace-root-switch call site SKIPS the issue. (Round 3 claimed both
routes; only the fresh-process one works.) The force-clear
deliberately does not delete that snapshot — it is the only remaining
path to a terminal event for a run that stays hung, and a PAUSED
snapshot additionally powers the pause-restore prompt.
terminal-latch              — ADR-017 Decision 5 latches and seals inside pipeline.notifyComplete's
terminal-seal-and-remove      terminal claim, and THE FORCE-CLEAR MUST NEVER CALL notifyComplete: a
dispatch the abort deadline gave up on is abandoned, not completed, and
routing it through the terminal claim would close a run that is still
alive. So neither half is performed here. A run that later settles
latches and seals through its own claim; one that stays wedged keeps its
NON-TERMINAL snapshot, which is deliberate — that file is the only
remaining path to a terminal event, and #44 orphan reconciliation emits
it at the next server start and removes it under the 14-day cap. The Go
scheduler path performs both directly in its terminal defer (#440); this
funnel is the extension side, where they are the claim's to do.
NOT APPLICABLE — Go-only by design (1):
lifecycle-decision-trace    — ADR 013 / #179; the extension path emits no trace on either funnel.
KNOWN EXPOSURE — Go-side late settlement, deliberately not fixed here. ADR-017 step 3 changed what
crosses the wire but NOT what the server does with it: every call a run makes now carries its run id,
and the server ACCEPTS AND IGNORES it until the step-4 re-key.
The TOMBSTONE is still extension-internal — it is not sent to Go, and the force-clear's only IPC calls
are queue.complete and autonomous.complete, neither of which touches the runtime registry. (The verb
that WOULD tell the server a dispatch is over is `pipeline.abandonRun`, and it lands in step 6.) A
force-cleared run that unwedges therefore still reaches a server that resolves by issue. Go keys
s.activeRuntimes by BARE ISSUE NUMBER, which is not a run identity, so if the operator has re-queued
the issue the dead run's notifyStageTransition / notifyComplete / notifyPhaseTransition /
notifyStageProgress / setPaused all resolve to the SUCCESSOR's runtime: its history record and
learning outcome can be written under the successor's RunID, and its completion deletes the
successor's runtime and its snapshot. Every one of those is present on main and is NOT a
regression introduced here — this change books the EXTENSION's terminal state and nothing else. Round
3 attempted a per-dispatch token on the Go side and it produced worse failure modes than it closed (a
single lost `initialized` message silently locked a live run out of every Go-side write, and a
token-carrying transition whose runtime was gone re-minted an identity for the dead run). Re-keying
Go's runtime registry by run identity is ADR-017 (#370) and is IN PROGRESS: step 3 (this change)
makes the extension emitter carry an identity the server can key on; STEP 4 is the re-key and the
verb requirements that actually close this exposure. Until step 4 merges, every sentence above
still describes the running system. See docs/decisions/017-runtime-identity-keying.md and
docs/GO_BINARY.md § Force-Clear Terminal Bookkeeping (Issue #307).
OTHER CONSEQUENCES this funnel takes ownership of naming:
* The issue becomes RE-DISPATCHABLE while a wedged process may still hold its worktree. Releasing
the queue mark and the Go seat is the whole point, and WorktreeManager keys one path per issue
number, so a successor is created in the tree the dead process may still be writing in. On main
the un-released `processing` mark serialized the two runs — i.e. the leak this fixes was also the
accidental interlock. Gating re-dispatch on the tree being verifiably free is still not done —
#305 gave the funnel a way to TELL the operator (the abandoned-dispatch card names what THIS
force-clear left behind and asks them to inspect it), but a card is a notification, not a gate.
* A reservation's `reservedSlots` entry is left in place on purpose: it is what stops a re-dispatch
from colliding with the still-running startSlot. A wedge that NEVER unwinds therefore holds that
reserved capacity for the life of the extension host, with no reaper. Unchanged from main, where
the same dispatch held the same reservation.
* A force-cleared slot's PipelineStateService is disposed while its run may still be in flight. That
is safe only because PipelineStateService.dispose() tears down emitters and disposables but leaves
`this.ipc` untouched, so the run's own notifyPipelineComplete still makes its call — which is what
the DELEGATED entries above depend on. A future dispose() that guarded subsequent calls would
silently delete the delegated history record and learning outcome without failing any test.
ADR-017 step 3 therefore puts NO guard in dispose() — and deliberately does NOT release the run
identity there either. An earlier cut of step 3 did release it, on the theory that a "recycled"
service would refuse the issue's next dispatch; no such recycling exists (createForWorktree returns
a NEW instance per dispatch and the singleton pairs dispose with resetInstance), so the only case
it changed was THIS one, and it changed it for the worse: the late notifyPipelineComplete would have
gone out with `runId: ""` and been refused `run_id_required` at step 4, so a late-settling
force-cleared run would have stopped writing the delegated history record and learning outcome —
two records silently no longer written, which is the failure class #370 exists to end. A disposed
service KEEPS its id, so its own terminal claim stays attributable and a step-4 server that is
re-keyed per run books the dead run under its own identity via Decision 5's terminal latch. The
release points are notifyPipelineComplete, clearPipeline and the keyed finallys at the dispatch
sites that minted — nothing else. Booking the DISPATCH terminal at force-clear time, rather than
waiting hours for a wedged run to deliver its own outcome, is still step 6's `pipeline.abandonRun`.

go.pathSpecific: By design extension-only: the Go scheduler's terminal defer runs in the same goroutine as its stage loop, so nothing else can declare the run abandoned while that defer is still owed. There is no Go-side force-clear, and therefore no second Go funnel to keep in parity. Go is BYTE-IDENTICAL to main for this change — see the KNOWN EXPOSURE paragraph in `accounting`.

behaviors.name: terminal-latch
behaviors.note: ADR-017 Decision 5 step 1c. Added to the Go path by #440; it was extension-path-only before, so a finished Go-scheduler run left a non-terminal snapshot on disk indefinitely.

behaviors.name: terminal-seal-and-remove
behaviors.note: ADR-017 Decision 5 step 4. Added to the Go path by #440. The path is the identity on both sides, so neither can remove a successor's snapshot.
